newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seeks more in Timan-Pechora oil deal - agency.
newsitem.headline: Russia seeks more in Timan-Pechora oil deal - agency.

text.p: Russia's Arkhangelsk region, home to a big planned oil deal with international consortium the Timan Pechora Co (TPC), is demanding that Russia have a bigger stake in the project, Interfax news agency said on Monday.
It quoted Felix Chimbulatov, deputy head of Russia's negotiating delegation to TPC, as saying that officials in the autonomous Nenets district of Arkhangelsk had made the demands.
He said a 20 percent share in TPC had been alloted to Russian companies Rosneft and Arkhangelskgeoldobycha, but said "such a share did not reflect Russia's interest in the project".
"Even if the 20 percent share is agreed, we must make it clear that Arkhangelskgeoldobycha has the right to at least a 10 percent share in the project," he said.
The demand could delay final approval of a production-sharing agreement with TPC, which must be approved by regional as well as federal authorities.
TPC was formed in 1994 and groups U.S. oil majors Texaco Inc, Exxon Corp and Amoco Corp, along with Norsk Hydro A/S of Norway.
TPC has agreed to Russian participation and talks are under way to include state oil holding company Rosneft and exploration outfit Arkhangelskgeoldobycha.
Texaco said last year that final approval of the agreement was likely in early in 1997.
The total contract area has potential recoverable reserves of 306 million tonnes (2.2 billion barrels) of oil.
It is estimated that capital investment of around $20 billion will be required over the life of the project.
